atoms.b: Distance-time graphs are useful for showing how the distance travelled by a person or object ((++changes stays_the_same)) over time.
The time always goes on the ((++bottom side)) axis.
In the graph above, the time is being measured in ((++minutes hours)).
The steeper the line in the graph, the ((slower ++faster)) the speed of the person or object .
This graph shows how many ((hours ++minutes)) it took for Mary to walk 1,000 metres to her school.

instruction.text: Select the distance scale of the graph.
Select the point above minute 8 on the graph.

atoms.b: After 8 minutes, Mary had walked ((800)) metres.

instruction.text: Select the point of the graph, where Mary had walked 400 metres.

atoms.b: It took Mary ((3)) minutes to walk 400 metres.

instruction.text: Select the part of the graph where Mary isn’t moving.

trainers.hint: To figure out when Mary isn’t moving, look at the part of the graph where the distance she has travelled doesn’t change over time.

atoms.b: Mary was stationary from minute ((4)) to minute ((7)).
